page.text:
When the codomain of a function $f : A \to B$ matches the domain of a
function $g : B \to C$, they can be chained into a single compound
mapping: the *composition* $g \circ f : A \to C$, defined by
$(g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))$.

Function composition is universally associative:
$(h \circ g) \circ f = h \circ (g \circ f)$. This associativity is the
bedrock of category theory, where functions serve as the prototypical
morphisms.
